title: Surface Cohesion PRD for Hosted Generation, Embeddings, and Rerank Endpoints
creator: Lina Chen
description: Align the behavior, contract, and launch readiness of the hosted generation (chat/completions), embeddings, and rerank endpoints so customers see consistent parameter semantics, predictable performance, and clear migration guidance. Deliver a single product playbook and acceptance criteria set that will be used for launch and post-launch telemetry.
background: Over the last year we shipped separate improvements to chat/completions, embeddings, and rerank surfaces. Each has minor differences in parameter names, response envelopes, and cost semantics that cause developer confusion and add support overhead. Customers building multi-feature flows (e.g., retrieve->embed->rerank->generate) need consistent integrations and predictable cost/latency behavior.
problem_statement: Inconsistent API surface and launch readiness across generation, embedding, and rerank endpoints increases SDK complexity, customer integration time, and surface-level bugs. We need a PRD that defines the minimal cohesive contract, required server and client changes, and an ops-safe rollout plan with measurable acceptance criteria.
goals: Unify core parameter semantics (timeout, max_tokens/length, top_k/top_p, model selection) across hosted generation, embeddings, and rerank endpoints
Define a single, documented response envelope format for metadata (model, token_count, cost_estimate) used by all surfaces
Provide launch-grade docs, SDK changes, and migration guides to minimize developer friction
Establish telemetry and SLOs to detect regressions after launch
Ship safe rollout with canary and automated fallback to current behavior for edge cases
non_goals: Major model architecture changes or new model onboarding (out of scope for this rollout)
Overhaul of Dedicated or Private deployment modes (this PRD targets hosted API only)
Changing pricing tiers or billing primitives (billing changes will be a separate initiative)
acceptance_criteria: API contract: All four surfaces (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) accept a harmonized parameter set documented in the public OpenAPI and SDKs
Response envelope: Every response includes standardized metadata keys: model, request_id, token_usage, approximate_cost (where applicable), and schema version header
Backward compatibility: Existing clients that do not opt into the new schema must continue functioning for at least 90 days; opt-in via request header 'X-RI-API-Version: v2'
SDKs: Official JS and Python SDKs expose the unified parameters and include migration helpers in the next release
Telemetry: Dashboards show per-route P50/P95 latency, error rate, tokens-per-request, and tokens-per-second with pre-launch baseline vs post-launch comparison
Load: System meets SLOs under target production traffic (95th percentile latency within 10% of current baseline) during a 2-hour peak test at 1.5x projected initial launch traffic
Rollout: Canary cohort (5% traffic) runs for 48 hours with automated rollback on error-rate delta > 0.5% absolute or latency regression > 20%
Docs: Public API docs, migration guide, and example multi-step flow (retrieve->embed->rerank->generate) published before general availability
Support readiness: Tier 1 playbook and incident runbook published and sign-off received from Support and Solutions Engineering
requirements: API: Add 'api_version' header and support 'v1' (legacy) and 'v2' (unified) semantics
Parameters: Normalize names (length vs max_tokens) and provide explicit deprecation mapping in docs
Response: Add standardized metadata envelope with 'token_usage' and 'approximate_cost' fields
SDK: JS and Python SDKs include compatibility layer that rewrites legacy params to unified names when using v2
Operational: Create per-route quotas and cost estimation tag in telemetry to enable cost breakdowns per-request
Testing: End-to-end tests that run multi-surface flows against staging that assert token counts and semantic outputs remain within tolerance
Canary infra: Traffic fraction routing and automated rollback hooks implemented in infra by ENG
Migration: Written migration guide with code snippets, changelog, and FAQ
launch_checklist: Design: Finalize API contract and example responses (doc link) and sign off from API review board
Engineering: Implement header-based versioning and SDK compatibility helpers; unit and integration tests passing
Performance: Run 2-hour 1.5x traffic soak and capture baseline metrics; pass SLO guardrails
Security/Privacy: Key review for 'approximate_cost' metadata to ensure no PII exposure; security sign-off obtained
Docs: Publish API docs, migration guide, and sample flows; update quickstarts
SDK Releases: Cut JS and Python SDK releases with migration helpers and announce deprecation timeline
Canary Deployment: Deploy to 5% of traffic and monitor for 48 hours per rollout plan
Observability: Create dedicated dashboard and alert set; hook into on-call rotation
Support: Publish runbook, escalate path, and train support squad on common migration issues
Legal/Compliance: Ensure new metadata fields are reflected in the data retention and processing docs
GA Decision: Product, Eng, Security, and Support sign-off on go/no-go checklist
rollout_plan: Phased rollout using header-based opt-in: (1) Internal devs and alpha customers (2) Public canary at 5% traffic for 48 hours with automated rollback triggers, (3) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% over 5 working days if metrics are stable. Deprecation window of legacy semantics will be communicated with a 90-day minimum notice before hard removal.
dependencies: ENG-72812 (runtime): header-based version parsing and per-route routing
ENG-73211 (sdk): compatibility helper libraries for JS/Python
ENG-73990 (obs): dashboards, cost tags, and alerting
risks: Client confusion if migration messaging is unclear — mitigated by migration guide and SDK helpers
Performance regressions caused by added metadata calculations — mitigated by performance testing and ability to disable cost estimation for v2 in emergencies
Billing/finance implications if approximate_cost is misunderstood — mitigate with clear language and non-billable estimates in initial release
Cross-surface edge cases where semantics cannot be perfectly aligned (e.g., rerank expects feature vectors) — document fallbacks and map behavior explicitly
notes: This PRD focuses on hosted API; Dedicated and Private products will be considered in a follow-up project after initial stabilization
We will use the header opt-in approach to minimize risk to existing customers and to collect early feedback
Approximate_cost is intentionally labeled 'approximate' and should not be used for billing decisions until finance signs off
